title: Malaysian exchange SINEGY says unauthorised access cost it estimated losses of RM131,780.16 from hot wallets
date_note: Fintech News Malaysia, published 25 Nov 2026, reports SINEGY dating the unauthorised access to 22 November.
geo_basis: Country only; Fintech News Malaysia names no city.
summary: Fintech News Malaysia reports that SINEGY, a Malaysian digital asset exchange, disclosed a security breach with estimated losses of RM131,780.16 in digital assets from its operational hot wallets, which it attributes to unauthorised access on 22 November. In its client update, SINEGY says it will cover the losses, customer account balances remained unchanged, and it expects to resume operations within 48 hours of the update.
plain: Malaysian exchange SINEGY says unauthorised access cost it estimated losses of RM131,780.16 from hot wallets. It says client balances are unchanged and it expects to resume operations within 48 hours of its update.
exec: SINEGY reports estimated losses of RM131,780.16 from hot wallets; it says it will cover them and expects to resume operations within 48 hours of its update.
action: SINEGY instructs customers not to transfer funds to deposit addresses issued before the incident.

sources.name: Fintech News Malaysia: SINEGY security breach

evidence.quote: has disclosed a security breach involving estimated losses of RM131,780.16 in digital assets.
The exchange expects to resume operations within 48 hours of the client update

validation.note: One publisher (Fintech News Malaysia) relaying SINEGY's own client update; the update itself was not read.
